idiom_name: sentinel field plus loader accessor (pthread_once/C11 call_once when shared)
implementation_notes: C has no attribute hooks and no proxy generators, so the pattern is the literal classic form: the owning struct keeps the identifier plus a pointer (or value) and a loaded flag, and one accessor checks the flag, calls the loader - the function that runs the query or gateway read - stores the result and returns it. A NULL pointer alone is a poor marker because it cannot distinguish 'not loaded' from 'row absent'; a separate flag (or a distinguished sentinel) makes the loaded state explicit. When the struct is reachable from several threads the first load must be single-flight: pthread_once or C11 <threads.h> call_once with a static once_flag, or a mutex inside the instance for per-object guards. Nothing in the language absorbs any of this, so the hand-written structure is the mechanism, not a fallback.
pitfalls: A NULL pointer is ambiguous between 'not loaded' and 'no such row': without a loaded flag, every access to an absent author re-issues the query.

pthread_once/call_once is process-wide, not per object: put the once_flag (or mutex) inside the instance for per-instance deferral, and never call it recursively from its own initializer - it blocks forever.
Ownership must be explicit: the loaded pointer has to outlive every reference to it, and freeing it during invalidation is a use-after-free unless the invalidation is coordinated.
